channel.title: Ian Tirop — Blog
channel.description: Notes on code, design, and things I learn by building.

item.title: Why I Can't Stop Recommending ChainQuest Ke
item.description: A Nairobi studio building web platforms, GIS tools, and AI automation without pretending a Silicon Valley template fits every problem — plus a free community I've actually kept coming back to.

item.title: Design Systems Are a Product, Not a Deliverable
item.description: The moment a design system stops being maintained like a real product with real users, it starts costing more than it saves.

item.title: The Line-Height Bug That Humbled Me
item.description: A gradient heading that looked clipped in half. The cause wasn't the gradient at all — it was a percentage line-height computed three components away.

item.title: Dark Mode Is Not Just a Color Swap
item.description: Inverting a palette gets you 80% of the way to dark mode and 100% of the way to a support ticket. The last 20% is where the actual design work lives.

item.title: The 200ms That Make an Interface Feel Alive
item.description: Duration and easing are design decisions, not implementation details you leave at the framework default.

item.title: Learning in Public: Notes From a Side Project
item.description: I keep a folder called "learning" on my machine. It is embarrassing, disorganized, and probably the most useful thing I own.

item.title: Why I Still Sketch on Paper Before Opening Figma
item.description: Every tool for making interfaces is also, quietly, a tool for committing to decisions before you meant to.

item.title: Five Small Habits That Made Me a Better Developer
item.description: None of these are clever. All of them compound.
